First reasoned review: Nuvolex executables and cookie-grant.sh
===========================================================

Method
------
Ran atomscan and cleave facts on all three original paths. Independently
decoded every .NET MethodDef body with dnfile/dncil, resolving call, field
and user-string tokens. Both assemblies decoded without method-body errors.
Traced entry points, spawned delegates and async MoveNext implementations.
No specimen was executed. Scanner scores and mutable filenames were not
used as behavioral proof. The supplied Triage reports were inaccessible
through the web reader; the conclusions below follow the specimen bytes.
Full IL, facts and scan outputs are in scratch/nuvolex-cookie-review and
scratch/fallout-review/facts-{0,1,2}.txt in this task's workspace parent.

c6855ef1ce8ed9c60a67e873c509d993c366b320419edcbe74cdfb8e99267c2e
----------------------------------------------------------------
Identification: self-labeled NanoCoreUltimate .NET surveillance/destructive
implant. This identifies its internal namespace, not independently verified
membership in the historical NanoCore family. Verdict: MALICIOUS.

Main (MethodDef 0x85, RVA 0x7bd4) schedules surveillance and disruptive
helpers and directly attempts BlockInput(true), Defender/service disabling,
hosts poisoning, shadow-copy deletion, IFEO hijacking and UAC bypass.
InstallPersistence (0x45) writes its own entry-assembly location into HKCU
and HKLM Run keys, copies itself into Startup, and creates logon and periodic
scheduled tasks. HookCallback (0x48) reads virtual-key values, attaches time
and foreground-window title and appends them to the shared keylog. The
StartKeylogger delegate (0x86) independently polls keys 1..255, tests 0x8000,
appends held keys and flushes the same log. Thus both hook and polling
collection findings are justified. FlushKeylog calls ToBase64 then SendToC2.

ClipboardMonitor's MoveNext reads clipboard text and creates CLIPBOARD
records; ContinuousScreenshot captures the desktop and serializes JPEGs.
Browser, wallet, Wi-Fi and file-stealing helpers actually enumerate/read the
indicated stores and form data records. USBWorm copies the entry assembly
and writes drive AutoRun configuration. Backdoor-account helpers launch net
user /add and localgroup administrators /add. These justify the existing
collection, credential-access, persistence and USB replication findings.

Important limits: ParseC2Url (0x27) sets _c2Domain to the empty string;
IsPlaceholder (0x28) always returns true. SendToC2 (0x37) appends locally to
Desktop/stolen_data_here.txt and temp_steal.log before this gate, then returns
without uploading. HTTP/AES API co-occurrence must not be labeled successful
exfiltration. EncryptAES (0x53) receives a 17-byte key and a 15-byte IV;
AES rejects these sizes. RealEncryption's MoveNext (0xbd) targets only
Desktop/TestFolder; transform failure precedes output creation and deletion.
The existing ransomware rule correctly says replacement ATTEMPT. Ransom
notes, policy lockout, wallpaper changes, recovery inhibition and security
tampering still provide concrete hostile behavior independently of crypto.
CorruptSystemFiles (0x82) opens core DLL paths with FileMode.Append (6),
FileAccess.Write (2), then appends random bytes: it does not overwrite their
headers. DumpLSASS (0x3b) only opens the process and reports handle access;
it does not dump LSASS memory. No new successful-encryption, LSASS-theft,
functional hollowing, or PDF-triggered worm claim was added.

dc7fb36988c78fe75b2d712fcc1ca7c8bd4224a1c0806e62d001583455f6fe5c
----------------------------------------------------------------
Identification: self-labeled NanoCoreFinal .NET surveillance/backdoor
implant masquerading as a Microsoft Windows Update service.
Verdict: MALICIOUS.

Main (0x33, RVA 0x2910) copies the executable, writes startup/Run/task
activation, configures fodhelper DelegateExecute hijacking, launches hidden
Defender-disable commands, creates an administrator account and starts the
surveillance modules. KeyloggerModule installs WH_KEYBOARD_LL; its callback
records key/window/time and SendLoop persists the buffer before reporting.
Clipboard/screenshot/file-stealing delegates read their sources, and the
browser module hands Chrome/Edge Login Data and Cookies files to SendFile.
The termination-critical call sets class 29 using a true by-reference value;
success depends on privilege/API results, not simply the API's presence.

StartReverseShell delegate (0x41, RVA 0x38bc) constructs TcpClient on port
5555, launches hidden cmd.exe with redirected stdin/stdout and starts two
explicit relay delegates (0x46/0x47) bridging its streams in opposite
directions. StartCommandExecutor delegate (0x42) GETs /cmd, executes the
response via cmd.exe /c, captures output and creates CMD_OUT records.
Its "download " verb exports an existing local file through SendFile; it
does not download and activate an external payload.

SendToC2 (0x3b, RVA 0x3c78) XORs bytes with key[index % key.Length], then
Base64-encodes and escapes them into an HTTP GET query. The existing
cil-modulo-key-byte-array-xor trait already detects this transform. Config
sets C2_DOMAIN to a complete http:// URL, while callers expect a bare host:
the TCP hostname and doubled-scheme HTTP URLs are malformed. Successful
remote control or exfiltration is not established for this configuration.
Local recording, unwanted persistence and security tampering remain hostile.

MicrophoneModule calls waveInGetNumDevs before attempting an invalid AxHost
PowerShell recording sequence. WebcamModule connects a VFW driver but sends
1061 (WM_USER+37), not FILE_SAVEDIB (WM_USER+25) or GRAB_FRAME (+60).
Therefore module names and report labels do not establish working audio or
camera capture. Added only a notable wave-input device-count API reference.
VFW constants checked against Microsoft's SDK Vfw.h:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/win32metadata/main/generation/WinSDK/RecompiledIdlHeaders/um/Vfw.h

98067d53be6be867c069b3f95809f014a04c012dafc657f548887b3cb34bbfbd
----------------------------------------------------------------
Identification: cookie-command PHP webshell / Apache installer.
Verdict: MALICIOUS. No trait edits needed for this specimen.

The shell script chmods /bin/sh to 6555, granting SUID and SGID permission
bits; writes a PHP passthru(urldecode($_COOKIE[...])) endpoint; and appends
an Apache Files PHP handler plus a static JavaScript asset alias pointing
to that endpoint. This is an unauthenticated operator-cookie-to-OS-command
sink concealed behind an asset URL, alongside a privileged-shell permission
grant. It warrants both existing hostile traits. The script does not reload
Apache, change shell ownership, or prove any shell preserves effective UID;
the current grant/install wording correctly avoids claiming those outcomes.

Trait and placement changes
---------------------------
Moved DecryptData word evidence from crypto/decrypt to binary/symbols/name;
it observes a chosen helper/interface name, not a decryption operation.
Preserved the PE/DLL word matcher, severity, confidence and platform scope,
including native images without CLR metadata. Updated all three exact
consumers. Audited broader crypto selectors: losing a mere name as crypto
capability evidence is intentional; the targets retain real cipher/transform
API evidence. For C# source, replaced lexical word matching with a parsed
function declaration under file/function; mentions in string literals no
longer claim a declared method. None of the three consumers accepts C#.

The binary/symbols/name leaf was at its 100-rule budget. Review found no
duplicate name matcher to consolidate. Its ten MSVC class RTTI descriptors
belong under binary/symbols/descriptor by the existing taxonomy contract.
Moved all ten together without changing matcher, bounds, severity, scope or
section restrictions. Updated every Gh0st exact reference and the existing
fixture check. No name/descriptor directory selectors consume these rules;
the only matching higher ancestor selector found was metadata/binary in a
timing rule and retains the same descendants. No new category or raised
directory budget was introduced.

Added a notable waveInGetNumDevs name reference under hardware/input/audio.
This is enumeration evidence only, with no microphone-collection or transfer
claim. Static controls cover binary/native helper names, parsed C# method
declarations versus strings, input versus output device APIs, all ten RTTI
descriptor matchers, a class-name near miss and the wrong section. These
fixtures are inert and are analyzed, never run. The pre-existing IoT/Gh0st
control suite checks preservation of its existing identity consumers.

Verification results
--------------------
20 new static positive/near-miss controls passed. The 14 existing IoT/Gh0st
controls passed with the relocated descriptor IDs. Final atomscan used the
edited working tree, slow mode, no rule update, and --follow=none. It retained
23 hostile / 14 suspicious findings for nano, 16 hostile / 1 suspicious for
new, and 2 hostile / 3 suspicious for the shell installer. The old decryption
name ID is absent; the binary metadata name fires for nano; the new audio
device-count reference fires for new. No specimen-specific exclusion or new
family attribution was added. Full repository validation is the final check.
